checks.check: The current predictions fail a schema, signal, or compatibility check.
checks.how: Inspect the latest traceback, sample predictions, output dimensions, and artifact loading logs.

checks.check: The claimed gain is no larger than variation in prior unchanged runs.
checks.how: Compare recent score deltas with the range or standard deviation of repeated runs using identical artifacts.

checks.check: Errors concentrate where the existing input representation loses available information.
checks.how: Inspect residuals by history length, text section, image detail, or signal window and compare with the raw inputs.

checks.check: A known noisy or shifted subgroup dominates the training errors.
checks.how: Break down held-out errors and label distributions by data source, label confidence, or entity subgroup.

checks.check: Learning curves show underfitting, overfitting, or unstable optimization despite correct inputs.
checks.how: Compare training and held-out loss curves with the model capacity, loss, and optimizer configuration.

checks.check: Available candidate predictors make complementary held-out errors.
checks.how: Align existing out-of-fold predictions and inspect residual correlations and candidate blend scores.

checks.check: Valid cached predictions exist and output mapping or blending is not yet compared on held-out data.
checks.how: Inspect prediction artifacts and the experiment log for missing aggregation or calibration baselines.

checks.check: Resource failures prevent the intended full pipeline or meaningful trials from completing.
checks.how: Locate out-of-memory errors, time-limit exits, and stages dominating the runtime profile.

checks.check: Related records, source shifts, or unstable target proportions undermine the present split.
checks.how: Inspect fold assignments against entity IDs, data sources, timestamps, and per-fold label histograms.

checks.check: Recent comparisons are confounded, noisy, or use a questionable metric.
checks.how: Read the edit diffs, repeat-run scores, metric implementation, and validation-to-external score pairs.

checks.check: Several recent trials failed to beat a reproducible baseline.
checks.how: Compare the trial ledger with the last saved best configuration, including the size and consistency of regressions.

checks.check: Target classes or target bins are unevenly distributed across the current folds.
checks.how: Count labels or fixed target bins per fold and compare their frequencies.

checks.check: Multiple rows share an entity, source, or topic that should be unseen at evaluation.
checks.how: Check identifiers and the task test-population definition, then count group overlap between train and validation.

checks.check: A recognizable source subgroup differs from the evaluation population.
checks.how: Compare source-specific label and feature distributions with known test metadata.

checks.check: The proposed subgroup allocation places the same row in training and validation.
checks.how: Intersect train and validation row IDs for every fold, including injected subgroup rows.

checks.check: A large fixed holdout substantially reduces fitting data after model choices are settled.
checks.how: Inspect training versus holdout counts and whether the holdout still controls early stopping or selection.

checks.check: Unchanged runs vary by as much as the proposed improvement.
checks.how: Inspect repeated scores and prediction differences with fixed input and checkpoint hashes.

checks.check: The public evaluation is tiny or disagrees with local model rankings.
checks.how: Use task-provided evaluation sizes and earlier paired local/external scores to assess resolution and ranking agreement.

checks.check: The compared versions changed multiple independent settings.
checks.how: Read version diffs for changes to checkpoints, features, seeds, and output transforms.

checks.check: Early stopping monitors a proxy, wrong dataset, or wrong metric direction.
checks.how: Inspect callback arguments and recompute the task metric on saved validation labels and predictions.

checks.check: The prediction unit or ordering of raw observations is not yet established.
checks.how: Inspect table keys, sample histories, timestamps, missingness summaries, and target joins.

checks.check: A reproducible regression followed a change and the prior working configuration is available.
checks.how: Compare the regression with repeat-run variability and inspect the saved baseline manifest.

checks.check: Several trials along the same lever show no reliable improvement.
checks.how: Read the trial ledger and compare best recent deltas with measured noise.

checks.check: Nearby tested parameter values bracket an improving region.
checks.how: Plot existing parameter-score pairs with noise estimates and identify a local interval worth refining.

checks.check: No complete pipeline has produced a valid measured prediction.
checks.how: Check execution logs and output artifacts for an end-to-end baseline.

checks.check: The candidate changes are coupled and a saved baseline permits later ablation.
checks.how: Identify dependencies such as rate with training duration, or a new modality with its required model, and verify the baseline artifacts.

checks.check: A new artifact or representation was introduced immediately before the failure.
checks.how: Compare the last working artifact manifest, model definition, and preprocessing configuration with the failing run.

checks.check: Execution completes but outputs are constant, implausible, or omit configured components.
checks.how: Inspect intermediate prediction statistics and execution counts for each fold and model.

checks.check: A traceback or absent output file identifies an execution dependency failure.
checks.how: Read the first exception and confirm whether the required final file exists.

checks.check: Checkpoint keys or tensor dimensions disagree with the reconstructed model.
checks.how: Use strict loading diagnostics and compare hidden sizes, head shapes, and state-dict prefixes.

checks.check: Inference transforms differ from those recorded for the training checkpoint.
checks.how: Diff resizing, filters, normalization, cropping, and feature-extraction configurations.

checks.check: Vocabulary, special tokens, or token positions differ from training.
checks.how: Compare tokenizer files, vocabulary length, special-token IDs, and any token-position extraction code.

checks.check: A downstream model receives different columns, encodings, or dimensions from those used in fitting.
checks.how: Compare ordered feature manifests, fitted encoder metadata, and the current matrix shape.

checks.check: Data or predictions were sorted, concatenated, or joined without an explicit identifier mapping.
checks.how: Compare ID sequences across every input frame and prediction vector.

checks.check: Configured model or fold counts exceed the number of accumulated predictions.
checks.how: Inspect loop counters, skip flags, accumulation indentation, and the final component manifest.

checks.check: The blend magnitude or shape changes unexpectedly with member count.
checks.how: Evaluate the arithmetic on a tiny known numeric array and inspect axes, divisors, and weight totals.

checks.check: Model or stage outputs are constant, placeholders, or derived from the wrong dataset.
checks.how: Inspect prediction variance, first examples, data IDs, and references passed between stages.

checks.check: Inputs, losses, or intermediate activations contain nonfinite values.
checks.how: Count NaNs and infinities at each boundary and identify the earliest occurrence.

checks.check: A custom objective edit preceded divergence or a catastrophic score loss.
checks.how: Compare analytical gradients and Hessians with numerical derivatives on a tiny sample and inspect return shapes.

checks.check: The error is a missing file or a read-only source path.
checks.how: List mounted files, resolve the configured path, and inspect the failing file operation.

checks.check: The failure is an import, missing symbol, or incompatible package version.
checks.how: Inspect the import traceback, module file locations, and bundled package versions.

checks.check: The error names an unsupported accelerator or mismatched tensor devices.
checks.how: Inspect model and tensor device fields and installed backend support.

checks.check: The first failure names an undefined variable, invalid keyword, type, or method.
checks.how: Reduce the failing call to a small example and compare it with the local function signature and object types.

checks.check: The computation completes but the expected prediction file is absent or invalid.
checks.how: Inspect output directory, writer execution, filename, columns, IDs, row count, and final prediction variable.

checks.check: Examples contain repeated structured observations that the current features collapse inadequately.
checks.how: Compare raw entity histories with the columns supplied to the model.

checks.check: Free text is the principal input and residuals vary with language or document structure.
checks.how: Inspect representative errors alongside text lengths, sections, vocabulary coverage, and existing feature families.

checks.check: Image or signal preprocessing discards potentially label-relevant detail.
checks.how: Compare raw examples and rendered model inputs with the task label scope and preprocessing parameters.

checks.check: An expanded or stale feature set is associated with worse validation or schema drift.
checks.how: Compare feature manifests and held-out scores before and after feature additions.

checks.check: There are multiple observations per entity but the model sees only a latest row or a narrow summary.
checks.how: Compare entity record counts with the current aggregation feature list.

checks.check: Recent changes or temporal order are not represented by full-history summaries.
checks.how: Inspect sorted histories and held-out errors for entities with changing trajectories.

checks.check: Related measurements have interpretable differences, ratios, or interactions absent from the feature set.
checks.how: Read column definitions and inspect candidate interaction distributions for valid denominators and plausible units.

checks.check: Stored precision, scaling, or noisy decimals are unsuitable for the learner.
checks.how: Inspect dtypes, unique-value counts, quantization, and the learner preprocessing requirements.

checks.check: Aggregations create missing values or model families differ in native NaN support.
checks.how: Count missing values after aggregation and inspect the configured learner input requirements.

checks.check: Available metadata has plausible target signal and is absent from the model.
checks.how: Compare held-out residuals by available source, category, or time fields and confirm those fields exist at inference.

checks.check: Cleaning may remove meaningful punctuation, spelling, or pretrained-tokenizer cues.
checks.how: Compare raw and normalized examples and inspect the checkpoint training preprocessing.

checks.check: Distinct text segments or known metadata are currently flattened without structure.
checks.how: Inspect input construction and tokenized examples against the task fields.

checks.check: The sparse representation omits common n-grams or has a large rare-token tail.
checks.how: Inspect vocabulary coverage, document frequencies, n-gram ranges, and matrix sparsity.

checks.check: Text quality or document organization is relevant but absent from current features.
checks.how: Inspect target definitions and errors by readability, sentence length, sections, or linguistic patterns.

checks.check: Current features capture counts but lack semantic information.
checks.how: Inspect existing feature families and available pretrained encoders, including embedding dimensions and memory requirements.

checks.check: Labeled neighbors or related-task labeled data are available without using evaluation labels.
checks.how: Inspect available training corpora, nearest-neighbor quality on held-out examples, and auxiliary-data provenance.

checks.check: Resizing removes label-relevant detail and compatible resolution checkpoints exist.
checks.how: Inspect raw and resized samples plus checkpoint input-shape metadata.

checks.check: Time-frequency detail is unresolved at the current transform settings.
checks.how: Inspect spectrograms alongside sampling rate, FFT window, hop length, and event duration.

checks.check: The current crop misses the labeled interval or includes mostly irrelevant context.
checks.how: Compare crop boundaries and window duration with annotations and training extraction code.

checks.check: Raw signals contain known interference, extreme amplitudes, or irrelevant frequency content.
checks.how: Inspect signal traces, amplitude quantiles, power spectra, and filter settings.

checks.check: Input scale or channel statistics differ from the pretrained model expectations.
checks.how: Compare input mean, spread, and dynamic range with the checkpoint preprocessing record.

checks.check: Channel layout or pseudo-image shape obscures available signal structure.
checks.how: Inspect tensor dimensions and rendered samples for channel identity, aspect ratio, and useful additional derived channels.

checks.check: A newly added feature family coincided with worse held-out performance.
checks.how: Compare the feature manifest and controlled validation scores before and after the addition.

checks.check: No stable relevance ranking exists for the current wide feature space.
checks.how: Inspect fold-level importance artifacts and their stability across folds or attribution methods.

checks.check: A ranking exists but its retention threshold is arbitrary or stale.
checks.how: Read selected counts, cap settings, and previous feature-count validation sweeps.

checks.check: Features were added or renamed after the saved selection file was generated.
checks.how: Compare feature-generation versions and names with the saved selection manifest.

checks.check: Expanded embeddings raise dimensionality sharply and validation has not improved.
checks.how: Compare embedding dimensions, source count, resource usage, and held-out scores before and after expansion.

checks.check: Sample quality, class proportions, or source coverage differ from the intended test population.
checks.how: Inspect label confidence, duplicate IDs, source frequencies, and task-described test sampling.

checks.check: The label definition includes censoring, ordinal levels, or group-specific ranking.
checks.how: Read the target columns and evaluation formula and inspect the current constructed targets.

checks.check: A neural model overfits and the input admits label-preserving perturbations.
checks.how: Compare train/validation curves and inspect whether candidate transformations preserve the annotated event or image finding.

checks.check: Duplicates, overlapping windows, unreliable labels, or mismatched sources are identifiable.
checks.how: Inspect entity/window overlap, label confidence, source metadata, and out-of-fold residual outliers.

checks.check: Additional labeled data with compatible input and label definitions exists.
checks.how: Compare auxiliary-source label semantics, coverage, quality, and distribution with the current training data.

checks.check: Unlabeled examples and a validated teacher or pseudo-labeled checkpoint are available.
checks.how: Inspect teacher confidence on held-out data and the pseudo-label generation recipe.

checks.check: A class or test-representative subgroup is underexposed during training.
checks.how: Compare sample frequencies and per-group errors with the task metric and expected test distribution.

checks.check: A minority group is small and within-class interpolation is meaningful in the feature space.
checks.how: Inspect class-specific neighbor distances, feature types, and prior oversampling results.

checks.check: Previous synthetic oversampling hurt the same held-out metric.
checks.how: Read controlled augmentation-on/off results under the present feature and validation setup.

checks.check: Targets contain event times and censoring indicators rather than fully observed outcomes.
checks.how: Inspect target schema and the censoring fraction.

checks.check: The evaluation separately scores predefined groups with different survival or target distributions.
checks.how: Read the metric formula and compare target distributions by its grouping variable.

checks.check: A scalar target transform or centering convention changed or remains untuned.
checks.how: Inspect target-construction code, inverse transforms, and prior transform-parameter comparisons.

checks.check: Labels are ordered discrete levels but the current model is plain regression.
checks.how: Inspect unique target values and the penalty for neighboring versus distant mistakes.

checks.check: Small image brightness or geometric changes preserve the target semantics.
checks.how: Inspect domain examples and the training transform code for valid invariances.

checks.check: The model relies on narrow time-frequency patches that may be absent at inference.
checks.how: Inspect spectrograms, occlusion sensitivity, or error cases with missing signal regions.

checks.check: Targets can be meaningfully mixed and current training overfits individual examples.
checks.how: Inspect soft-label semantics, training/validation divergence, and existing mixup settings.

checks.check: A correctly implemented backbone or learner has plateaued across local tuning.
checks.how: Review controlled trials on the current family and available compatible pretrained or alternative learner candidates.

checks.check: A minimal head or fusion rule discards useful backbone or branch information.
checks.how: Inspect model forward code and branch dimensions and compare errors with representation ablations.

checks.check: The active learner is a tree model with capacity or convergence problems.
checks.how: Read the learner configuration and tree training/validation curves.

checks.check: The active component is neural and its optimization or loss is suspect.
checks.how: Inspect neural training curves, gradient stability, epochs, scheduler, and objective definition.

checks.check: A compatible alternative pretrained backbone or size is available.
checks.how: Inspect artifact metadata, required tokenizer or input shape, and existing controlled backbone comparisons.

checks.check: Available pretraining data is substantially closer to the task domain than the current initialization.
checks.how: Read checkpoint provenance and compare it with task inputs.

checks.check: The features are tabular or fixed vectors and the current tree implementation has plateaued.
checks.how: Inspect the feature matrix and recent depth, rate, and regularization trials.

checks.check: A meaningful input representation is not served well by the current architecture.
checks.how: Compare raw signal, spectral image, or fixed embedding structure with the current model input and available alternatives.

checks.check: The backbone feeds a minimal, inappropriate shared, or oversized head.
checks.how: Inspect the head layers, per-target parameter sharing, and training/validation behavior.

checks.check: Only one hidden layer or pooling statistic is used despite variable-length or multi-layer information.
checks.how: Read the forward pass and inspect the tensors discarded before the output layer.

checks.check: An auxiliary target or discretized version of the main target is available.
checks.how: Inspect label derivability from training targets and whether independent validation can assess the main-task effect.

checks.check: Multiple informative branches are merged by a lossy or untested rule.
checks.how: Inspect branch ablations, equal-dimension averaging, concatenation dimensions, and corresponding checkpoint training.

checks.check: The head overfits or varies markedly across seeds.
checks.how: Inspect train/validation gaps, seed-specific scores, and current dropout configuration.

checks.check: Trees appear capacity-limited or increased capacity has begun to overfit.
checks.how: Compare training and validation curves across existing depth and leaf-count settings.

checks.check: Training error improves while validation worsens with the current feature set.
checks.how: Inspect learning curves and row/column sampling and penalty settings.

checks.check: Learning rate changed without a corresponding convergence budget.
checks.how: Compare rate, maximum rounds, selected iteration, and whether validation was still improving at the cap.

checks.check: Stopping occurs before convergence, on the wrong set, or with excessive patience.
checks.how: Inspect the monitored dataset/metric and training logs around the selected iteration.

checks.check: Many manually set parameters lack isolated evidence of benefit.
checks.how: Review the parameter history against default values and controlled comparisons.

checks.check: Training is unstable or converges poorly at the current learning rate.
checks.how: Inspect batch losses, gradients, warm-up behavior, and earlier rate trials.

checks.check: The training loss stalls at a schedule transition or under the current optimizer.
checks.how: Inspect the learning-rate trace, optimizer state, and loss curve around transitions.

checks.check: Training ends while validation improves or continues well beyond its best epoch.
checks.how: Inspect epoch-level validation curves and stage-specific checkpoint metrics.

checks.check: The training loss poorly represents the ranking, distribution, or ordinal evaluation objective.
checks.how: Compare the mathematical training objective with the evaluation formula and prior loss ablations.

checks.check: A component lacks consistent fold training or reproducible held-out predictions.
checks.how: Compare its train/validation indices, preprocessing scope, saved checkpoints, and data-loader logic with other components.

checks.check: Existing members mostly share the same architecture, features, targets, or training randomness.
checks.how: Compare the member manifest and out-of-fold residual correlations.

checks.check: There are untested, weak, or recently changed members in the current pool.
checks.how: Review individual scores, marginal ablations, and member changes since the last weight search.

checks.check: Several compatible saved runs or training-stage artifacts are available.
checks.how: List checkpoint metadata and their held-out metrics without loading them into the final blend.

checks.check: Current members share a family and their held-out errors are highly correlated.
checks.how: Inspect architecture metadata and an aligned out-of-fold residual correlation matrix.

checks.check: A relevant modality, feature set, or preprocessing view is not represented.
checks.how: Compare member input manifests with available raw data and known representation ablations.

checks.check: Alternative valid target transforms or training recipes yield different held-out errors.
checks.how: Compare candidate recipe metadata and aligned out-of-fold predictions.

checks.check: Compatible unused fold or snapshot predictions are already available.
checks.how: Inspect checkpoint manifests, fold identities, and the current average membership.

checks.check: Training seeds produce materially different held-out predictions.
checks.how: Compare existing independent seed runs and verify inference repeats alone are not identical.

checks.check: Compatible checkpoints from one weight-space trajectory are saved.
checks.how: Check architecture identity, training trajectory, and availability of snapshots suitable for weight averaging.

checks.check: The candidate has not yet produced verified standalone predictions.
checks.how: Inspect candidate inference logs, prediction statistics, and any standalone held-out score.

checks.check: A functioning candidate has plausible complementary errors but no marginal-blend result.
checks.how: Compare aligned out-of-fold residuals and confirm it has not yet been tested alongside the intact baseline.

checks.check: A member is weak, redundant, or associated with a regression.
checks.how: Inspect prior leave-one-out results, component errors, and when it entered the pool.

checks.check: A new compatible checkpoint can replace a specific weaker slot.
checks.how: Compare the slot and candidate training recipes and existing standalone quality evidence.

checks.check: Removing formerly useful members caused a reproducible regression.
checks.how: Compare the saved successful member manifest with the current reduced pool and its scores.

checks.check: Other model components or aggregation rules changed since the last membership test.
checks.how: Diff component artifacts and aggregation settings against the last ablation record.

checks.check: Several runs or fold checkpoints have matching architecture and preprocessing.
checks.how: Inspect checkpoint metadata and their local validation scores.

checks.check: Artifacts differ mainly by training stage or stopping criterion.
checks.how: Read checkpoint epoch, stage, and selection-metric metadata.

checks.check: Both full-data-trained and fold-trained artifacts are available.
checks.how: Compare the training-row and fold metadata for available checkpoints.

checks.check: Prediction scales or the aggregation domain differ across members.
checks.how: Inspect raw score ranges, probability sums, activations, and the current blending expression.

checks.check: The same valid prediction pool has only an arbitrary weight allocation.
checks.how: Compare current weights with component quality and previous equal-weight or optimized-blend results.

checks.check: A downstream learner uses base predictions or embeddings as input features.
checks.how: Inspect the meta-feature manifest and whether valid out-of-fold training inputs exist.

checks.check: The task requires discrete ordered outputs or labels occupy a few repeated levels.
checks.how: Inspect the target value histogram and official output and metric specification.

checks.check: Prediction units, probability calibration, or subgroup residual bias need correction.
checks.how: Compare output ranges and per-class or per-group residual plots with the task target definition.

checks.check: The input has valid alternate views that the current inference uses only once.
checks.how: Inspect training transformations and domain symmetries or available context windows.

checks.check: The metric rewards ordering and members have different score scales.
checks.how: Read the metric definition and inspect per-member score histograms and calibration ranges.

checks.check: Members expose logits and probabilities for a distribution-based metric.
checks.how: Inspect output activations and probability row sums, and identify where normalization occurs relative to averaging.

checks.check: Model families contribute unequal numbers of fold or seed predictions.
checks.how: Count predictions per family and derive each family's effective weight from the current formula.

checks.check: Aligned leakage-free out-of-fold predictions exist for a simple learned blender.
checks.how: Verify every meta-training prediction excludes its own row and compare meta-feature count with the calibration sample size.

checks.check: An established stacker has plateaued and its model class or penalty is untested.
checks.how: Inspect held-out meta-learner errors and previous linear, kernel, or tree comparisons.

checks.check: Probability saturation may make arithmetic averaging overly dominated by confident members.
checks.how: Inspect member probability distributions and held-out comparisons of raw and transformed predictions.

checks.check: Only tiny or noisy calibration data are available relative to meta-model flexibility.
checks.how: Compare calibration size and subgroup coverage with meta-feature count and tuning history.

checks.check: Members differ reliably in quality or complementary error structure.
checks.how: Compare aligned out-of-fold scores and correlations, rather than standalone public scores alone.

checks.check: Equal weighting matches tuned weights within measured score noise.
checks.how: Compare previous equal-weight and tuned-weight results with repeat variability.

checks.check: Prior unconstrained or signed fits suggest a component can cancel correlated error.
checks.how: Inspect fitted coefficients and independent validation, and confirm the output is not required to remain a convex probability mixture.

checks.check: Component strengths differ consistently by an observable class or subgroup.
checks.how: Compare per-class or per-group held-out errors and verify the condition is available at inference.

checks.check: Member quality, count, augmentation, or scaling changed after weights were selected.
checks.how: Compare the current component and transform manifest with the weight-search manifest.

checks.check: Component prediction scales differ substantially or contain heavy outliers.
checks.how: Inspect means, standard deviations, medians, interquartile ranges, and extreme predictions.

checks.check: Training meta-features include in-sample predictions or inconsistent fold assignments.
checks.how: Join prediction provenance with training indices and verify that each row was excluded from the generating model's fit.

checks.check: Additional aligned auxiliary outputs provide signal not captured by existing base scores.
checks.how: Inspect held-out correlation or incremental predictive value of available embeddings, logits, or auxiliary outputs.

checks.check: The meta-feature pool has grown while validation stagnates or regresses.
checks.how: Compare pool versions and ablation results and inspect redundancy among prediction columns.

checks.check: The ordinal metric is sensitive to cutpoints and representative held-out predictions are available.
checks.how: Compare naive rounding errors with target levels and inspect out-of-fold coverage of each class.

checks.check: Optimized thresholds have unstable or worse independent performance than simple rounding.
checks.how: Compare held-out results across folds or previous threshold variants with the clip-and-round baseline.

checks.check: Known target frequencies are stable enough to support a distribution-matching comparison.
checks.how: Compare label frequencies across training sources and held-out folds with the stated test sampling.

checks.check: Continuous predictions correspond to a small set of repeated target levels.
checks.how: Inspect unique labels, prediction gaps, and per-target histograms.

checks.check: Subgroups exhibit different residual-to-label mappings and are observable at prediction time.
checks.how: Compare held-out calibration curves by group and audit the source of inference-time group assignments.

checks.check: Existing binning collapses a column or creates many artificial ties.
checks.how: Count distinct predictions per column before and after binning and inspect the metric's tie convention.

checks.check: The checkpoint or ensemble changed since calibration was fitted.
checks.how: Compare the threshold-fit prediction manifest with the current checkpoint and blend manifest.

checks.check: Outputs have the wrong units, activation, range, or probability sum.
checks.how: Compare output summaries and training target transforms with the submission specification.

checks.check: Some components rank risk in the opposite direction.
checks.how: Check each output convention against its target transform and its signed held-out association with outcomes.

checks.check: Valid probabilities show systematic confidence or per-class mass bias.
checks.how: Inspect held-out reliability curves, predicted class mass, and observed label distributions.

checks.check: A systematic additive or reference-relative bias remains in valid predictions.
checks.how: Inspect held-out mean residuals or predictions of fixed reference examples under the same model.

checks.check: A high-precision auxiliary classifier or metadata rule identifies a predictable error subset.
checks.how: Measure rule precision and subset residuals on held-out data and confirm the rule uses inference-available information.

checks.check: A previously helpful post-processing step has not been reassessed after upstream changes.
checks.how: Compare model/ensemble versions with the last isolated post-processing on/off trial.

checks.check: The proposed global monotone rescaling cannot change the metric's ordering.
checks.how: Check that the metric is purely rank-based and the transform introduces no clipping, rounding, or changed blending.

checks.check: A deterministic flip or sensor symmetry preserves the label.
checks.how: Inspect the domain meaning of each axis or channel and the training augmentation record.

checks.check: Multiple valid windows or compatible resolutions cover the same prediction target.
checks.how: Compare label scope, available context, and checkpoint preprocessing for each view.

checks.check: Repeated forward passes intentionally vary and prior stochastic-view evidence is promising.
checks.how: Compare saved per-pass predictions and inspect active-dropout or random-transform code.

checks.check: Repeated passes should be identical but differ because training-mode layers or random transforms remain active.
checks.how: Inspect model evaluation mode, dropout and batch-normalization state, RNG use, and per-pass outputs.

checks.check: The proposed augmentation changes signal meaning or previously hurt this branch.
checks.how: Inspect branch-specific augmentation ablations and whether axes represent time or frequency rather than interchangeable space.

checks.check: Peak memory or per-batch throughput is the limiting resource.
checks.how: Inspect allocation failures and stage-level memory and runtime logs.

checks.check: Repeated trials recompute unchanged work or fail late after expensive training.
checks.how: Profile the trial cycle and identify reusable artifacts or the smallest execution that reproduces the issue.

checks.check: Hard-coded paths, duplicated model code, or unrecorded settings cause configuration drift.
checks.how: Compare code paths and artifact manifests across recently inconsistent runs.

checks.check: The full data or feature table cannot fit, but complete entities can be processed independently.
checks.how: Inspect memory use by data stage and whether entity-level aggregation crosses proposed partition boundaries.

checks.check: Memory accumulates across successive model loads.
checks.how: Track allocated memory before and after each model and find live references retained past their final use.

checks.check: Large feature matrices use wider dtypes than their range and required precision justify.
checks.how: Inspect per-column dtype, min/max, precision requirements, and memory footprint.

checks.check: Peak memory occurs inside one forward pass and scales with batch size.
checks.how: Compare failure point and allocation logs for existing batch sizes.

checks.check: Model activations dominate memory and reduced precision is supported by the inference stack.
checks.how: Inspect dtype/backend support and any prior full- versus mixed-precision prediction comparisons.

checks.check: A metric, transform, or repeated device transfer dominates elapsed time.
checks.how: Profile the relevant stage and compare available equivalent implementations on a small fixed sample.

checks.check: The current task is checking correctness and failures occur after expensive work.
checks.how: Identify the smallest data slice and training settings that still execute the failing path.

checks.check: Only downstream settings change while upstream features or predictions remain identical.
checks.how: Compare experiment diffs with feature/model artifact hashes and stage runtimes.

checks.check: Some folds or training stages are complete but session limits prevent finishing the rest.
checks.how: Inspect saved checkpoint manifests for completed and missing stages or fold indices.

checks.check: The next evaluated run must use the complete selected configuration but debug shortcuts remain enabled.
checks.how: Audit fold limits, early exits, stage flags, and output-generation guards against the final configuration.

checks.check: Adding model variants repeatedly requires editing duplicated code and shared globals.
checks.how: Inspect duplicated inference functions, per-model preprocessing differences, and recent integration bugs.

checks.check: Dead code or training-only paths obscure a stable inference pipeline.
checks.how: Compare active dependencies and a saved reference prediction before removing unused code.

checks.check: Identical code can load different artifacts or settings across runs.
checks.how: Inspect mutable checkpoint directories, file discovery order, seed handling, and saved weight/configuration manifests.

checks.check: Some component files are missing or current exception handlers silently inject placeholders.
checks.how: Inspect file-existence checks, caught exceptions, fallback arrays, and denominator adjustment.
